headline: Population structure shapes epidemic thresholds and strain coexistence
label: Structured Epidemic Model Dynamics
summary: Late-January 2026 preprints extend epidemic models to behavioural heterogeneity, airborne spread and multi-strain coinfection in structured hosts.
synthesis: The dominant thread is that structure in contact, space, behaviour and host population governs epidemic thresholds and strain persistence. HeSIR extends SIR with bimodal behavioural heterogeneity, yielding a closed-form threshold and a mapping to an effective contact network. The coinfection SIS analysis treats N strains in structured hosts, using a global replicator equation to predict coexistence from invasion fitness. The chemotaxis-inspired PDE defines a spatially aware reproduction number for airborne transmission, supported by stabilized numerics and simulations for Lombardy and Georgia. The phenology-structured tree model, reduced to two ODEs, is an ecological item that shares only the emphasis on threshold-type dynamics under environmental forcing, contrasting warming and drought. What is new is the explicit analytical reduction of structure to tractable threshold or coexistence criteria, although the items do not share a single modelling framework.
